h1: Laemchabang City Hotel — a clean, good-value city hotel near Laem Chabang Port in Tungsukla, Si Racha
intro: If you're coming to work, dealing with the industrial estate, or stopping over before heading in or out of Laem Chabang Port around Si Racha, and you want a hotel with clean rooms, a decent amount of space, easy parking, and a price that won't spiral — Laemchabang City Hotel is a name people who work around here know well · It's a 3.5-star city hotel, a 6-floor building with as many as 128 rooms in Tungsukla subdistrict, Si Racha district, that leans on its location near the port and industrial estate, good-value rooms, and the Sweet Lemon restaurant rather than being a beachfront resort like Bang Saen or Pattaya · There's no swimming pool here and it isn't right on the beach, but it gives you rooms that many people say are bigger and cleaner than the price suggests, a location close to markets and restaurants, and easy travel to the port, the industrial estate, and Space Inspirium · Prices start from about THB 750/night · Scored 8.3 from 141 reviews on Traveloka and 9.1 on Trip.com.

body.html: Who Laemchabang City Hotel suits — the overview — To put it as simply as possible, Laemchabang City Hotel is a city hotel for people coming to Laem Chabang mainly for "work reasons" · It isn't a seaside resort that brings you here for a holiday, and it isn't a small boutique selling design · It's a 128-room hotel in a 6-floor building in Tungsukla subdistrict, Si Racha district, positioned as a base for people who need to get in and out of Laem Chabang Port and the industrial estates in this area · The groups it suits best, going by genuine reviews, are business travelers, company staff coming for meetings or site visits, ship crew and port workers, and technicians and project teams staying several nights — plus families visiting Space Inspirium who want somewhere nearby at a budget price · Another group that says it's impressed is travelers who need a one-night stopover on the way to or from the eastern region, because it's easy to drive in from the motorway and Sukhumvit Road · What brings people back is the feeling of "paying this much but getting a room bigger and cleaner than expected," a combination that isn't common among budget hotels in industrial areas · On the flip side, if you're after a holiday vibe, a pool, or sea views, this may not be the answer, and you'd be better off moving over to Bang Saen or Pattaya instead.

Location and getting around — This is the main reason people choose to stay at Laemchabang City Hotel · The hotel sits at 53/325 Moo 9, Tungsukla subdistrict, Si Racha district, an area surrounded by Laem Chabang Port and the Laem Chabang industrial estate · The distances people ask about most are that it's about 2.7 kilometers from the Laem Chabang industrial estate and about 2.4 kilometers from Space Inspirium (the Space Krenovation Park), both a few minutes' drive away · Harbor Laemchabang mall, with a cinema, restaurants and a supermarket, is not far, about a 10–15 min drive · Anyone wanting to head into Si Racha town or Central Si Racha is about 11 kilometers away · On airports: it's about 57 kilometers from U-Tapao Airport (UTP) and about 100 kilometers from Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK), with an easy drive via the motorway · Around the hotel there are made-to-order restaurants, convenience stores, and markets to walk around for food, which many reviews praise as "easy to find a meal" · The honest caveat is that this is an industrial zone — the main roads carry a fair number of trucks and container lorries, so the surroundings feel more like a working town than a tourist town, and without your own car you may have to rely on taxis or ride-hailing apps, which can be harder to get at certain times than in the town center.

"Came to work at the industrial estate and stayed here several nights. The room was clean, the bed comfortable, and parking was easy without competing for a spot · At this price it's really good value for the Laem Chabang area, and finding food around the hotel is convenient too."

Room types and decor — Laemchabang City Hotel has 128 rooms in total in a 6-floor building, split across several tiers · The most-booked rooms are the Deluxe Double Room (large bed) and Deluxe Twin Room (two single beds), about 24 sqm, most of which are on floors 5–6 · Moving up, there's the Premier Room, which is more spacious and better decorated, and the Junior Suite for those who want more living space · The decor is a simple contemporary style that prioritizes practicality over luxury, in easy-on-the-eye tones · Every room has air conditioning, a fridge/minibar, blackout curtains, a work desk, an electric kettle, a phone, and bathroom amenities with a hairdryer · The point many reviews agree on is that the rooms are bigger than expected for the price, clean, and the beds are comfortable, suiting people staying several nights to work · For anyone who needs to take online meetings or work in the room, the work desk and Wi-Fi that actually works help make a working stay easier · One thing worth knowing is that some reviews say the furniture and certain details are starting to show their age, and that some angles in the website photos look a touch newer than the real thing, so set your expectation to "clean, functional, good value" rather than brand-new in every corner · Anyone who wants a quiet room should ask for a higher floor that doesn't face the main road.

Facilities (and the pool question) — Let's be straight from the start: Laemchabang City Hotel has no swimming pool · This is a city hotel focused on staying for work and travel, not a leisure resort, so if a pool is non-negotiable for your trip, this won't be the right pick · But on the essential facilities, the hotel covers what you need for real use: a 24-hour front desk, a lift, free parking, free Wi-Fi everywhere, laundry/dry-cleaning service, luggage storage, and a terrace · An advantage for business guests is the business center and meeting rooms, which can host small to mid-sized seminars or meetings — a reason many companies choose this as both team accommodation and an in-house meeting venue · The free, spacious parking is another thing reviews mention often, because people driving themselves or arriving as a team in several cars don't have to worry about parking · Overall the facilities here are the "right-sized for the job" kind — nothing fancier than necessary, but everything someone coming to work or stopping over actually needs.

Food and the Sweet Lemon restaurant — The hotel's main restaurant is Sweet Lemon, serving Thai and general food, mainly open for breakfast and lunch · Going by genuine reviews, breakfast here is "about right" — enough choice to fill you up for the start of a working day, but not a varied buffet like a big hotel · Many people note that the breakfast options are fairly limited, which lines up with the food score sitting around 7.6 on booking platforms · The upside is that the hotel's location makes up for this a lot, because nearby there are made-to-order restaurants, rice shops, and convenience stores within easy reach, so many guests choose to head out for food at other meals easily · For workers getting back to the hotel late, having restaurants and convenience stores nearby is important, and it's a point reviews praise as "convenient for finding a meal" · In short, in-hotel food at Laemchabang City Hotel isn't the reason to come and eat, but it's a usable extra for breakfast — for other meals, it's worth making the most of the shops around the hotel.

Service — Service at Laemchabang City Hotel is a point where opinions vary quite a bit · Those who praise it say the staff are friendly, helpful, and look after regular guests well, especially with parking, holding luggage, and helping coordinate meeting rooms for corporate clients · The 24-hour front desk lets people heading in and out of the port or working shifts check in and out flexibly · But to be fair, some voices in the reviews mention service at the front desk that isn't as smooth as it should be at certain times — sometimes communication or responses are a bit slow, especially when occupancy is high · This is something you'll find at mid-sized hotels that take both nightly guests and corporate groups at the same time · Overall, the level of service is still considered good for the price, and isn't a problem that keeps most people from coming back.

Voices from genuine reviews (both praise and gripes) — Pulled together from Trip.com, Traveloka, Booking.com and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: good value and well-suited to the Laem Chabang area, rooms clean and bigger than expected, comfortable beds, a location close to markets and restaurants that makes finding food easy, free and spacious parking, a location near the port and industrial estate that's convenient for workers, and friendly staff · On Trip.com it scores as high as 9.1, with the location category around 9.4 · On the caveat side: what comes up is fairly limited breakfast options, front-desk service that isn't smooth at certain times, some website photo angles looking newer than the real thing, and some furniture starting to show its age · On top of that, the Tripadvisor score is fairly low because the reviews are few and old, while the booking platforms with more recent reviews rate it well · These gripes are mostly things you won't feel let down by once your expectations are set right, because this is a budget hotel focused on value and location, not a luxury hotel.

"Spacious, clean room and a great price for Laem Chabang · My only gripe is that breakfast doesn't have much to choose from, but there are plenty of rice shops around the hotel, so you can walk out and eat outside — not a problem."

Price comparison and value — The starting price for a Deluxe room is about THB 750/night in normal periods, and can climb to around THB 900–1,200 when occupancy is high, such as during seminars or projects at the industrial estate · Premier rooms and the Junior Suite sit higher depending on size and the time of year · Compared with hotels of the same level in the Laem Chabang–Si Racha area, Laemchabang City Hotel feels good value among accommodation for workers and people passing through, especially when you factor in the spacious rooms, free parking, the location near the port and industrial estate, and the in-house meeting rooms · If you're coming to Laem Chabang mainly for work and don't need a pool or sea views, the money you spend here pays you back in convenience and right-sized comfort · But if it's a holiday trip where you want a resort feel, the same budget might go further on accommodation over in Bang Saen.

Things to know before booking — A few things help make the stay smoother · One, check-in starts at 2:00 PM and check-out is 12:00 PM as standard, but the front desk is open 24 hours, so if you arrive late or leave very early for the port, you can give advance notice · Two, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a higher floor that doesn't face the main road with trucks passing · Three, the hotel has no swimming pool — if you want a pool, choose somewhere else · Four, breakfast has limited options, so if you're a fussy eater or like a varied buffet, plan to head out to the shops around the hotel as well · Five, if you're coming as a team or hosting a meeting, contact the hotel about meeting rooms and group rates in advance for a better deal · Six, compare prices across several platforms (Agoda / Booking / Trip.com / Traveloka) before booking, because prices shift with events at the industrial estate, and choose free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet.

Summary — From all the genuine reviews, Laemchabang City Hotel is the hotel that suits people coming to Laem Chabang for work, dealing with the port and industrial estate, or stopping over on the way, who want a clean, spacious room at good value · Rooms bigger than the price, free parking, a location near the port, the industrial estate, and Space Inspirium, plus in-house meeting rooms, make it a tidy choice for business guests and travelers · If you're looking for a holiday vibe, a pool, or sea views, this isn't the answer, and you should consider a resort over in Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · But for a trip focused on convenience near Laem Chabang Port on a manageable budget, with clean rooms and service that's right-sized for the job — Laemchabang City Hotel is the choice that matches that need at good value, and it's why it still scores well with people who come for exactly what the hotel is.
